item.title: Crimes Against Nature: Forum Criticism Team - Junior Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Raddishdude, per the required forum guidelines, please use the standardized template for concepts found here: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-13282684/required-reading:how-to-use-this-forum-ideas

Please remember to be mindful that the combined text of the last four sections1 of the template may not exceed 400 words. For convenience, authors can check wordcount using this site: https://wordcounter.net/

Once you have reviewed the guidelines, please edit your post to the correct format rather than creating a new thread, and if you are having trouble editing, click the "edit" function under the "options" tab to the lower right of your post. Please feel free to then reach out to a reviewer for your concept: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-13282692/how-to-get-more-reviews

Footnotes
1. Elevator Pitch, Central Narrative, Hook/Attention-Grabber, and Additional Notes

item.title: The Song of Your Life (Seeking Greenlights): Re: The Song of Your Life (Seeking Greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Hi there!
As a fan of musical theatre and sound tracks this sounds like a really cool idea. I wonder if this radio can just react to the mood or it if can influence it as well, maybe it takes a liking to some researcher and when they are sad the radio plays cheerful music to try to lift their spirits.
The "I don't have a song but I used to" concept is what really sold it to me. It really brings the SCP from a curiosity to a character to be explored and to have a narrative arc.
This is a nice pitch, has potential for a nice story.

item.title: The Dover Demon: Re: The Dover Demon
item.content:encoded:
1) First, you're about 50 words over and need to fix some capitalization problems.

2) You need to decide which events he's been at and focus on those. The problem is that too many "immortal historian" tales feature someone who has met every historical figure and been to every major event; even done with someone who is obviously lying about certain events, and therefore it becomes a game to figure which are lies and which aren't, it can quickly get annoying. Especially as The Foundation has better sources.

3) This would sort of be fun to adapted into a series of tales, possibly framed as a way to haze for new researchers.

item.title: The Dover Demon: The Dover Demon
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Comedy/History

Elevator Pitch: SCP-X is the creature known as The Dover Demon. SCP-X is a small humanoid with bright white eyes lacking pupils, with a large skull and and no mouth, however it is able to speak, with its face moving as if it is speaking. It also has 4 long fingers. SCP-X is also able to become invisible, to hide itself from others. SCP-X is very friendly (and rather humorous) and likes interacting with trusted individuals. It typically walks on its two hind legs, but if it is running, runs on four legs.

+ Central Narrative
- Hide

The main focus of the article will be centered around an interview conducted with SCP-X shortly after its recovery. SCP-X is asked about where its from. This leads to a brief explanation that he was born in a cave, and that once he was around 19 he left his family. He then set off to explore the world and its numerous wonders. (Which he states was around 1600 he would typically spend long amounts of time wandering the world and exploring new places.) He soon traveled to England, undetected because of his ability to become invisible. He claims to have wandered the streets of Great Britain, before leaving England on the mayflower, and arriving in America.

He claims to have secretly settled with the pilgrims, and lived in Massachusetts from 1620-1780, where he claims to have witnessed several witch trials, and the Boston Massacre in which he attempted to aid colonists that had been shot by British soldiers. He claims that he is the dog in the painting by Paul Revere, and that Paul Revere is a "denier of his existence". He then claims to have traveled west, and spent the rest of the 1700's travelling America.

SCP-X claims to have traveled back to New England in the early 1800's, where he indirectly causes the destruction of a textile mill when he attempted to operate one of the machines, but instead somehow caught it on fire, causing the entire mill to burn down.

He also briefly covers how he was travelling through dover in the 1970's, lining up with the "Dover Demon sightings" made by William Bartlett, John Baxter, and Abby Brabham. SCP-X's life was for the most part uneventful from then until its capture by the foundation.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I think the attention grabber that the foundation literally has a little guy telling tales about the Mayflower and the industrial revolution, which he's witnessed. (and possibly the unique idea around this concept?)

Additional Notes: I've always had some interest in the Dover Demon, and thought of this idea that might fit him. Give me your critiques and tell me what you think!

item.title: "Long" Beach California (Seeking Feedback): Re: "Long" Beach California (Seeking Feedback)
item.content:encoded:
Hey there BUCKSHOT74, I’ll be critting your idea today!
Note that I am not an official reviewer, so take what I say with a grain of salt. With that said, let’s begin the crit!

+ Open Section-by-Section
Woooooosh

Elevator Pitch

So it’s a beach 60 miles1 south of Long Beach where the water seems 80-90 yards2 away, yet never gets closer. To be honest, I’m not too keen on this idea (by itself). It isn’t very interesting in my opinion (all it is is a beach where the water doesn’t get closer), and seems to simply be the opposite of SCP-2684. However, if a good narrative is applied to it, it still could work.

Central Narrative

The narrative here consists of the Foundation sending out people to find out what’s up with the beach, and that’s about it. Some people die, they find some writing (which you proceed to not tell us about), and there’s a vague notion of a tall, mysterious entity that kills everyone who saw it. Personally, I don’t really like this. There isn’t any deeper narrative or explanation as to why the beach appeared, it just boils down to people being killed, which I find uninteresting.

Hook/Attention Grabber

The dry-drowning premise is unique[…]

Unfortunately, it isn’t. SCP-1812 is an excellent example of a dry-drowning premise that is in-theme, where we see the dry-drowning is due to the perceived higher gravitational pull on Earth’s water. In your idea, we don’t have an explanation as to why the first D-Class suddenly drowned, they just did. Oddly, they drowned at 8kms out rather than much sooner (which would make sense with the water depths of the average beach), and I’d like an explanation.

Also, as I explained earlier, the narrative is kind of boring, so the audio logs wouldn’t keep the reader entertained.

+ Open General Thoughts
I don’t know about this

The idea is (in my opinion) relatively boring, the narrative isn’t interesting and doesn’t give any explanation for the beach or entity, and the unique concept in your hook isn’t unique. Unless you overhaul the narrative to this, I don’t think your concept would survive on the mainsite.

Anyway, that’s it for my crit today. Thanks for reading, and I hope this helps!

Footnotes
1. Metric, not imperial, is the system used on the Site.
2. Metric.

item.title: I Am Requesting A Greenlight On A Concept: Re: I Am Requesting A Greenlight On A Concept
item.content:encoded:
Hello Dr Camero! lets take a look :)

SAND

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Elevator Pitch: A katana, longbow, and samurai armor, with anomalous properties, crafted using an unknown element.

What are the anomalous properties? what does the skip do? does it have a purpose? what is this 'unknown element'?-what part does this have in the narrative? what about this will make me as the reader care?

-Currently the skip doesn't really show anything outwardly interesting or unique, as it doesn't have much going for it other than the effects (which themselves are quite vague). As a result, the skip comes across as a bit cliched and dime a dozen, as there are already a fair few amount of sword and weaponry related articles on the main-site, and this concept (in its current state) doesn't seem to bring anything new to the table. Which in turn, makes it hard for me get invested in the idea, or confident that it would work in its current state.

The narrative:

Central Narrative: A katana that is forged from an unknown smith, a longbow with arrows that will seek the wielders target, and armor that is practically unbreakable.

This is closer to additional info than a story, there isn't any sort of setup, middle act, payoff or conflict shown here. How will the current idea fit into a narrative?- what would the article look like? What direction will the story take? are there any characters? how does the Foundation get involved? whats the main conflict? whats everything building up to? what will make me as the reader invested in this?

I would highly recommend starting development on a narrative, as they can help with audience engagement and can further explain the skip. Modern audiences tend to favour skips with a narrative, which has lead to them more or less becoming the standard. The narrative doesn't need to be a long winded saga, short stories can work very well if done right.

Hook:

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The sword can drain exact amounts of blood, and heal wounds perfectly once the blood is lost. The longbow can shoot arrows at unnatural speeds and the arrows can always hit their mark. The armor is from a time period that didn't exist when it was made, and can't be destroyed.

This isn't really much of a hook, it's more or less a bunch or specific effects which alone don't keep my interest as there isn't much behind them. What part does this play in the story? whats their purpose?

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight

If you would like me review this (or any concept) further, then please feel free to send me a PM or ask via IRC. Response times generally range from 2-12 hours over PMs. If your looking for additional critiques in general, then I would highly recommend contacting the butterfly squad :)

Cheers,

-RED

item.title: The Song of Your Life (Seeking Greenlights): The Song of Your Life (Seeking Greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Musical

Page Layout (Optional): Basic layout

Elevator Pitch:
-SCP is a sentient vintage ham radio that produces various forms of music to living things that enter its radius.
-The music in-question is based off the person's history, personality, how other people view them and in the case of other SCPs or other anomalous entities, their abilities. It can also play music to what would otherwise fit the scenario in-question (if its a containment breach its going to sound out chase music mixed in with the leitmotifs of the other SCPs that are part of the breach, etc, etc.)
-The SCP can teleport to a place that is having a suitably dramatic moment and play said music or otherwise to a person that it has played music to before and is 'bored.'

Central Narrative: As above with potentially exploring other SCP's stories and personalities through the radio's music. Eventually (I don't really know how planned interviews and addendum later down the SCP's life-line works) I'm planning for a researcher to try and ask the SCP questions, the SCP answers in a semi-convoluted way.

Standard questions apply and then… the researcher will go to ask 'do you have a song of yourself?'

The radio will reply 'no' but will than go onto say, 'but I'm sure I did have one, but I don't anymore.'

And like… that could go down so many routes, who took it? Where is it now? How do we get it? What happens when the SCP gets its 'song' back?

Does the Foundation fulfill its request? The SCP probably has some hints in its memory of where the song once was and that can go into tales or more interviews and mission ops and lot of other things.

So that's a narrative I've come up with.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I've looked over other SCPs for a while now and while there are a couple that do involve music, there are none that I could find that involve the SCP finding the theme song of basically anything in existence… except itself. Of a most important note including other SCPs that could delve into one's personality or backstory through usage of music.

Additional Notes: No particular concerns right now.
